description: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. Search, scrape and access 550+ data providers through one API.

--- # **🔥 Firecrawl** **Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. 🔥** You can use Firecrawl three ways. This repo holds the code for Firecrawl Local and the self-hosted server, along with SDKs that work with all three. - **[Firecrawl Local](#firecrawl-local).** Run Firecrawl on your own machine as one binary that turns websites into clean markdown, plugs into your AI agent as an MCP server and serves the Firecrawl API on localhost. - **[Firecrawl Cloud](#firecrawl-cloud).** Use the hosted service at [firecrawl.dev](https://firecrawl.dev/?ref=github) for everything Local does at scale with nothing to run, plus search and the 550+ data providers in [Firecrawl Alexandria](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev) for far more knowledge than scraping alone. - **[Self-hosting](#self-hosting).** Deploy the full Firecrawl server from `apps/api` with its own queues, workers and databases on your own infrastructure. _Pst. Hey, you, join our stargazers :)_ --- ## Firecrawl Local [Firecrawl Local](apps/local) scrapes, crawls and maps from your own machine without a database, queue or container, and it reaches Firecrawl Cloud when your AI agents need search or Alexandria. It installs from crates.io. You need Rust and a C compiler, which on macOS means `xcode-select --install` and on Debian or Ubuntu means `build-essential`. ```bash cargo install firecrawl-local ``` If you don't have Rust, [Firecrawl Cloud](#firecrawl-cloud) runs the same scrape with nothing to build and no signup. ```bash npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest scrape https://firecrawl.dev ``` Scrape a page and print its markdown. ```bash firecrawl-local scrape https://firecrawl.dev --markdown ``` Crawl a site and save one markdown file per page. ```bash firecrawl-local crawl https://docs.firecrawl.dev --limit 50 --out ./pages ``` List every URL on a site. ```bash firecrawl-local map https://firecrawl.dev ``` Pages that need JavaScript render in the Chrome or Chromium already on your machine, and PDFs and Office documents are parsed locally too. Without a browser, static pages still work and a page that needed one comes back with a warning. ### Add it to your AI agent `init` finds Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex on your machine and adds Firecrawl Local to each one as an MCP server. It backs up every config file first, and the MCP server itself needs Node.js 22 or newer. ```bash firecrawl-local init ``` Restart your AI tool afterwards. Its scrape, crawl, map and batch scrape tools run on your machine, and the other Firecrawl tools go to Firecrawl Cloud. ### Run the Firecrawl API on localhost `serve` answers the Firecrawl v2 API on port 3002, so code written for Firecrawl runs against it unchanged and local routes need no API key. ```bash firecrawl-local serve ``` Point any Firecrawl SDK at it by setting the API URL. ```python from firecrawl import Firecrawl app = Firecrawl(api_url="http://localhost:3002") print(app.scrape("https://firecrawl.dev").markdown) ``` The [Firecrawl Local README](apps/local) covers every command and option, the security defaults for `serve` and running it in Docker. Move to [Firecrawl Cloud](#firecrawl-cloud) when you need structured JSON, Interact, the Agent or scale beyond one machine. --- ## What runs where | Feature | Firecrawl Local | Firecrawl Cloud | |---------|-----------------|-----------------| | [Scrape](#scrape) | Markdown, HTML, raw HTML and links | Adds structured JSON, summaries, screenshots and browser actions | | [Crawl](#crawl), [Map](#map) and [Batch Scrape](#batch-scrape) | ✅ | ✅ | | PDFs and Office documents | ✅ | ✅, plus [Parse](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/parse) for uploaded files | | [Search](#search) | Through Firecrawl Cloud, no account needed | ✅ | | [Alexandria](#alexandria) | Through Firecrawl Cloud after `firecrawl-local login` | ✅ | | [Interact](#interact), [Agent](#agent) and [Monitor](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/monitoring) | | ✅ | Scraping, crawling and mapping run on your machine. By default a single-page scrape that won't load there is fetched by Firecrawl Cloud instead and marked `"source": "firecrawl-cloud"` in the result. Those Cloud calls work without an account at a limited rate, and `firecrawl-local login` puts them on your Firecrawl account. Set `FIRECRAWL_CLOUD=off` to keep everything on your machine. --- ## Firecrawl Cloud Firecrawl Cloud runs everything Firecrawl Local does at scale, with no browser or machine of your own to look after. It also gives your AI agents access to far more knowledge than scraping alone, with search, Alexandria, Interact and Agent all through a single API. - **Works on the real web.** Covers 96% of the web, including JS-heavy pages and dynamic apps ([see benchmarks](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/the-worlds-best-web-data-api-v25)). - **Fast.** P95 latency of 3.4s across millions of pages, built for real-time AI agents and dynamic apps. - **LLM-ready output.** Clean markdown, structured JSON, screenshots and more, so your AI agents spend fewer tokens. [Firecrawl Keyless](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/firecrawl-keyless-launch) gives you 1,000 free credits a month with no API key or signup across MCP, the CLI and the API. For an API key, sign up at [firecrawl.dev](https://firecrawl.dev) and try it in the [playground](https://firecrawl.dev/playground). ### Search Search the web and get full content from results. ```python from firecrawl import Firecrawl app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY") search_result = app.search("firecrawl", limit=5) ```
Node.js / cURL / CLI **Node.js** ```javascript import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl'; const app = new Firecrawl({apiKey: "fc-YOUR_API_KEY"}); app.search("firecrawl", { limit: 5 }) ``` **cURL** ```bash curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/search' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "query": "firecrawl", "limit": 5 }' ``` **CLI** ```bash firecrawl search "firecrawl" --limit 5 ```

Node.js / cURL / CLI **Node.js** ```javascript import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl'; const app = new Firecrawl({ apiKey: "fc-YOUR_API_KEY" }); app.scrape('firecrawl.dev') ``` **cURL** ```bash curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{ "url": "firecrawl.dev" }' ``` **CLI** ```bash firecrawl scrape https://firecrawl.dev firecrawl https://firecrawl.dev --only-main-content ```

# Firecrawl v2.11.0
 
## Improvements
 
- **Firecrawl Research Index** — Added a specialized index for agentic AI/ML research: search across 3M+ arXiv papers and the GitHub code behind them (issues, merged PRs, and READMEs, refreshed daily), fetch a paper's details or related work, and check claims against full text. It has state-of-the-art recall on arXivQA, outperforming the next best provider by 18% at comparable cost. Available via the API, SDKs, MCP, and CLI.
- **Keyless access for core endpoints** — Use `/scrape`, `/search`, `/interact`, and `/parse` without an API key from official MCP, CLI, and SDK clients.
- **Automatic PII redaction** — Added a `redactPII` option that strips personal and sensitive data like names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, and secrets out of scraped content before it's returned.
- **`deterministicJson` format** — Added a format that returns structured JSON without running an LLM on every request. Firecrawl generates a reusable extractor for your schema and caches it per site, so repeat scrapes are cheaper and return consistent results.
- **Video discovery on any page** — Expanded the `video` format to find videos on any page, not just supp

releases.body:
# Firecrawl v2.10

## Improvements

- **`/parse` endpoint** — Upload local files (PDF, DOCX, DOC, ODT, RTF, XLSX, XLS, HTML) up to 50 MB and get back clean, LLM-ready Markdown, JSON, or a summary. Tables and reading order are preserved, with full Zero Data Retention support for enterprise plans. Available in JS, Python, Go, Rust, Java, .NET, PHP, Ruby, and Elixir SDKs.
- **Lockdown Mode** — Set `lockdown: true` on `/scrape` to serve results exclusively from Firecrawl's index with zero outbound requests and zero data retention by default. Gated outbound paths include HTTP fetches, robots.txt, audio downloads, and media. Available in every SDK, the CLI (`--lockdown`), and MCP.
- **`question` format** — Pass a natural-language prompt to `/scrape` and get a grounded, hallucination-free answer back in `data.question`. Runs on a managed model chain with automatic fallback, prompt-injection isolation via XML tagging and zero-width-space escaping, and up to 100x fewer tokens per call.
- **`highlights` format** — Returns the exact sentences, code blocks, and table rows on a page that match your query. Consecutive sentences re-join into paragraphs, code lines wrap in fenced blocks wit

releases.name: v2.9.0
releases.body:
# Firecrawl v2.9.0

## Improvements

- **Browser Interaction via `/interact` endpoint** — Scrape a page, then call `/interact` to take actions on it — click buttons, fill forms, navigate deeper, or extract dynamic content. Describe what you want in natural language via `prompt`, or write Playwright code (Node.js, Python) and Bash (`agent-browser`) for full control. Sessions persist across calls, with live view and interactive live view URLs for real-time browser streaming. Persistent profiles let you save and reuse browser state (cookies, localStorage) across scrapes. Available in JS, Python, Java, and Rust SDKs.
- **`query` format** — Added `query` format to the `/scrape` endpoint — pass a natural-language prompt and get a direct answer back in `data.answer`.
- **`audio` format** — Added `audio` format option to scrape responses, returning audio output as a field on the document.
- **`onlyCleanContent` parameter** — Added `onlyCleanContent` parameter to the `/scrape` endpoint, which strips navigation, ads, cookie banners, and other non-semantic content from markdown output.

🔥 Firecrawl

Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. 🔥 You can use Firecrawl three ways. This repo holds the code for Firecrawl Local and the self-hosted server, along with SDKs that work with all three.

  • Firecrawl Local. Run Firecrawl on your own machine as one binary that turns websites into clean markdown, plugs into your AI agent as an MCP server and serves the Firecrawl API on localhost.
  • Firecrawl Cloud. Use the hosted service at firecrawl.dev for everything Local does at scale with nothing to run, plus search and the 550+ data providers in Firecrawl Alexandria for far more knowledge than scraping alone.
  • Self-hosting. Deploy the full Firecrawl server from apps/api with its own queues, workers and databases on your own infrastructure.

Pst. Hey, you, join our stargazers :)

Firecrawl Local

Firecrawl Local scrapes, crawls and maps from your own machine without a database, queue or container, and it reaches Firecrawl Cloud when your AI agents need search or Alexandria. It installs from crates.io. You need Rust and a C compiler, which on macOS means xcode-select --install and on Debian or Ubuntu means build-essential.

cargo install firecrawl-local

If you don't have Rust, Firecrawl Cloud runs the same scrape with nothing to build and no signup.

npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest scrape https://firecrawl.dev

Scrape a page and print its markdown.

firecrawl-local scrape https://firecrawl.dev --markdown

Crawl a site and save one markdown file per page.

firecrawl-local crawl https://docs.firecrawl.dev --limit 50 --out ./pages

List every URL on a site.

firecrawl-local map https://firecrawl.dev

Pages that need JavaScript render in the Chrome or Chromium already on your machine, and PDFs and Office documents are parsed locally too. Without a browser, static pages still work and a page that needed one comes back with a warning.

Add it to your AI agent

init finds Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Codex on your machine and adds Firecrawl Local to each one as an MCP server. It backs up every config file first, and the MCP server itself needs Node.js 22 or newer.

firecrawl-local init

Restart your AI tool afterwards. Its scrape, crawl, map and batch scrape tools run on your machine, and the other Firecrawl tools go to Firecrawl Cloud.

Run the Firecrawl API on localhost

serve answers the Firecrawl v2 API on port 3002, so code written for Firecrawl runs against it unchanged and local routes need no API key.

firecrawl-local serve

Point any Firecrawl SDK at it by setting the API URL.

from firecrawl import Firecrawl

app = Firecrawl(api_url="http://localhost:3002")
print(app.scrape("https://firecrawl.dev").markdown)

The Firecrawl Local README covers every command and option, the security defaults for serve and running it in Docker. Move to Firecrawl Cloud when you need structured JSON, Interact, the Agent or scale beyond one machine.

What runs where

Feature Firecrawl Local Firecrawl Cloud
Scrape Markdown, HTML, raw HTML and links Adds structured JSON, summaries, screenshots and browser actions
Crawl, Map and Batch Scrape ✅ ✅
PDFs and Office documents ✅ ✅, plus Parse for uploaded files
Search Through Firecrawl Cloud, no account needed ✅
Alexandria Through Firecrawl Cloud after firecrawl-local login ✅
Interact, Agent and Monitor ✅

Scraping, crawling and mapping run on your machine. By default a single-page scrape that won't load there is fetched by Firecrawl Cloud instead and marked "source": "firecrawl-cloud" in the result. Those Cloud calls work without an account at a limited rate, and firecrawl-local login puts them on your Firecrawl account. Set FIRECRAWL_CLOUD=off to keep everything on your machine.

Firecrawl Cloud

Firecrawl Cloud runs everything Firecrawl Local does at scale, with no browser or machine of your own to look after. It also gives your AI agents access to far more knowledge than scraping alone, with search, Alexandria, Interact and Agent all through a single API.

  • Works on the real web. Covers 96% of the web, including JS-heavy pages and dynamic apps (see benchmarks).
  • Fast. P95 latency of 3.4s across millions of pages, built for real-time AI agents and dynamic apps.
  • LLM-ready output. Clean markdown, structured JSON, screenshots and more, so your AI agents spend fewer tokens.

Firecrawl Keyless gives you 1,000 free credits a month with no API key or signup across MCP, the CLI and the API. For an API key, sign up at firecrawl.dev and try it in the playground.

Search

Search the web and get full content from results.

from firecrawl import Firecrawl

app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY")

search_result = app.search("firecrawl", limit=5)

const app = new Firecrawl({apiKey: "fc-YOUR_API_KEY"});

app.search("firecrawl", { limit: 5 })

-H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{
  "query": "firecrawl",
  "limit": 5
}'

CLI

result = app.scrape('firecrawl.dev')

# Firecrawl

Firecrawl helps AI agents search, scrape, and interact with the web.

## Features
- Search: Find information across the web
- Scrape: Clean data from any page
- Interact: Click, navigate, and operate pages
- Agent: Autonomous data gathering

Interact

Scrape a page, then interact with it using AI prompts or code.

from firecrawl import Firecrawl

app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY")

result = app.scrape("https://amazon.com")
scrape_id = result.metadata.scrape_id

app.interact(scrape_id, prompt="Search for 'mechanical keyboard'")
app.interact(scrape_id, prompt="Click the first result")
Node.js / cURL / CLI

Node.js

import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl';

const app = new Firecrawl({apiKey: "fc-YOUR_API_KEY"});

const result = await app.scrape("https://amazon.com");

await app.interact(result.metadata.scrapeId, {
  prompt: "Search for 'mechanical keyboard'"
});
await app.interact(result.metadata.scrapeId, {
  prompt: "Click the first result"
});

cURL

# 1. Scrape the page
curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{"url": "https://amazon.com"}'

# 2. Interact with the page (use scrapeId from step 1)
curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/scrape/SCRAPE_ID/interact' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-d '{"prompt": "Search for mechanical keyboard"}'

CLI

firecrawl scrape https://amazon.com
firecrawl interact exec --prompt "Search for 'mechanical keyboard'"
firecrawl interact exec --prompt "Click the first result"
{
  "success": true,
  "output": "Keyboard available at $100",
  "liveViewUrl": "https://liveview.firecrawl.dev/..."
}

Agent

Describe what you need, and our AI agent searches, navigates and retrieves it with no URLs required.

curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/agent' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "Find the pricing plans for Notion"
  }'
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "result": "Notion offers the following pricing plans:\n\n1. Free - $0/month...\n2. Plus - $10/seat/month...\n3. Business - $18/seat/month...",
    "sources": ["https://www.notion.so/pricing"]
  }
}

Pass a schema to get structured data back.

from firecrawl import Firecrawl
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import List, Optional

app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY")

class Founder(BaseModel):
    name: str = Field(description="Full name of the founder")
    role: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Role or position")

class FoundersSchema(BaseModel):
    founders: List[Founder] = Field(description="List of founders")

result = app.agent(
    prompt="Find the founders of Firecrawl",
    schema=FoundersSchema
)

print(result.data)

The Agent documentation covers starting URLs, effort levels and the spark-2 model.

Crawl

Crawl an entire website and get content from all pages.

curl -X POST 'https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/crawl' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer fc-YOUR_API_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://docs.firecrawl.dev",
    "limit": 100,
    "scrapeOptions": {
      "formats": ["markdown"]
    }
  }'

It returns a job ID, and the SDKs poll it for you until the crawl finishes.

{
  "success": true,
  "id": "123-456-789",
  "url": "https://api.firecrawl.dev/v2/crawl/123-456-789"
}

Map

Discover all URLs on a website instantly.

from firecrawl import Firecrawl

app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY")

result = app.map("https://firecrawl.dev", search="pricing")
# Returns URLs ordered by relevance to "pricing"

Batch Scrape

Scrape many URLs at once.

from firecrawl import Firecrawl

app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY")

job = app.batch_scrape([
    "https://firecrawl.dev",
    "https://docs.firecrawl.dev",
    "https://firecrawl.dev/pricing"
], formats=["markdown"])

for doc in job.data:
    print(doc.metadata.source_url)

Alexandria

Firecrawl Alexandria gives your AI agents 550+ data providers in one library (250M+ people, 75M+ companies, 41M+ research papers), plus specialized indexes and the live web, through one API, MCP or CLI. AI agents discover a tool alongside their web results, inspect its inputs and pricing, then run it to get structured data. Discovery is free, and running a tool uses the credits listed on it.

Install it in your AI agent from alexandria.firecrawl.dev, or see the Alexandria documentation for CLI, MCP, SDK and API usage. Alexandria runs on Firecrawl Cloud, and Firecrawl Local can use it once you sign in with firecrawl-local login.

Connect your AI agent

The Firecrawl CLI gives your AI agent every Cloud tool with one command. It works with Claude Code, Antigravity, OpenCode and more, so restart your agent after installing.

npx -y firecrawl-cli@latest init --all --browser

Any MCP client can connect with this config.

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "firecrawl-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "firecrawl-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY": "fc-YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}

An AI agent can sign up its user and get an API key by fetching the onboarding skill.

curl -s https://firecrawl.dev/agent-onboarding/SKILL.md

See the Skill and CLI documentation for every command, and firecrawl-mcp-server for MCP.

SDKs

The SDKs cover every Firecrawl feature and poll async jobs for you. They work with Firecrawl Cloud, and with Firecrawl Local once you set the API URL to http://localhost:3002.

Python

pip install firecrawl
from firecrawl import Firecrawl

app = Firecrawl(api_key="fc-YOUR_API_KEY")

# Scrape a single URL
doc = app.scrape("https://firecrawl.dev", formats=["markdown"])
print(doc.markdown)

# Use the Agent for autonomous data gathering
result = app.agent(prompt="Find the founders of Stripe")
print(result.data)

# Crawl a website (automatically waits for completion)
docs = app.crawl("https://docs.firecrawl.dev", limit=50)
for doc in docs.data:
    print(doc.metadata.source_url, doc.markdown[:100])

# Search the web
results = app.search("best AI data tools 2024", limit=10)
print(results)

Node.js

npm install firecrawl
import { Firecrawl } from 'firecrawl';

const app = new Firecrawl({ apiKey: 'fc-YOUR_API_KEY' });

// Scrape a single URL
const doc = await app.scrape('https://firecrawl.dev', { formats: ['markdown'] });
console.log(doc.markdown);

// Use the Agent for autonomous data gathering
const result = await app.agent({ prompt: 'Find the founders of Stripe' });
console.log(result.data);

// Crawl a website (automatically waits for completion)
const docs = await app.crawl('https://docs.firecrawl.dev', { limit: 50 });
docs.data.forEach(doc => {
    console.log(doc.metadata.sourceURL, doc.markdown.substring(0, 100));
});

// Search the web
const results = await app.search('best AI data tools 2024', { limit: 10 });
results.data.web.forEach(result => {
    console.log(`${result.title}: ${result.url}`);
});

Self-hosting

Firecrawl Local is the easiest way to run Firecrawl yourself. If you really want the full Firecrawl server with its own queues, workers and databases, all of it still lives in this repo and you can run it on your own infrastructure. If you'd rather not run anything yourself, Firecrawl Cloud gives you every feature with no setup.

The server runs with Docker Compose alongside Redis, PostgreSQL and a browser service, and the self-hosting guide takes you from checkout to your first scrape.

SELF_HOST.md lists the services and settings for the revision you checked out, and larger deployments can start from the Kubernetes manifests or the Helm chart. Alexandria runs on Firecrawl Cloud, so the self-hosted server does not include it.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An API service that crawls websites and turns them into clean, LLM-ready markdown data.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Firecrawl is a highly robust web crawling and scraping API designed to perfectly extract data from websites and format it for Large Language Models. Instead of returning raw, noisy HTML, it processes complex web pages, single-page applications, and PDFs to generate clean, structured Markdown. The engine natively handles rendering JavaScript, managing rate limits, circumventing IP blocks, and navigating pagination. It also features agentic capabilities, allowing it to interact with pages by clicking, scrolling, and executing dynamic actions. This drastically reduces the boilerplate developers must write to prepare web data for AI ingestion.
keyFeatures: Markdown Conversion: Automatically strips out HTML noise and converts page content into clean, structured Markdown ready for LLM ingestion.
JavaScript Rendering: Executes client-side JavaScript to ensure dynamic content and modern single-page applications are fully scraped.
Automated Crawling: Follows links intelligently to crawl entire domains without requiring complex configuration or recursive logic.
Rate Limit Management: Incorporates built-in throttling and rotating proxies to prevent the scraper from being blocked by target websites.
Agentic Interaction: Allows developers to issue prompts that instruct the scraper to click, search, and navigate interactive web pages before extraction.
Extensive Media Parsing: Parses and extracts textual content from web-hosted PDFs, DOCX files, and other document formats.
